literal: Paul, a slave of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, having been set apart unto the gospel of God,
prose: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,

literal: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy scriptures
prose: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy scriptures

literal: concerning his Son, the one having come of the seed of David according to flesh,
prose: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,

literal: the one having been marked out [as] Son of God in power according to [the] spirit of holiness from resurrection of dead ones, of Jesus Christ our Lord,
prose: who was declared Son of God in power, according to the spirit of holiness, by resurrection from the dead—Jesus Christ our Lord,

literal: through whom we received grace and apostleship unto obedience of faith among all the nations, on behalf of his name,
prose: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations, on behalf of his name,

literal: among whom you also are called ones of Jesus Christ,
prose: among whom you also are called of Jesus Christ,

literal: To all those being in Rome, beloved of God, called holy ones: grace to you and peace from God [our] Father of us and of Lord Jesus Christ.
prose: To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

literal: First indeed I thank the God of me through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because the faith of you is proclaimed in [the] whole world.
prose: First of all, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

literal: For witness of me is God, to whom I render service in the spirit of me in the gospel of the Son of him, how unceasingly mention of you I make,
prose: For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness that I constantly make mention of you,

literal: always at the prayers of me, asking if somehow now at last I shall be prospered, in the will of God, to come to you.
prose: always in my prayers, asking that somehow, at last, I may now succeed by God's will in coming to you.

literal: For I long to see you, in order that I might impart some spiritual gift to you, unto the strengthening of you,
prose: For I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you, for your strengthening,

literal: And this is, to be mutually encouraged among you, through the faith of one another, both of you and of me.
prose: That is, that we may be mutually encouraged among you through the faith that is in one another, both yours and mine.

literal: Not I want but you to be ignorant, brothers, that many times I purposed to come to you, and was prevented until the now, in order that some fruit I might have also in you, just as also in the rest [to the] nations.
prose: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I intended to come to you, but was prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as also among the rest of the Gentiles.

literal: To Greeks both and to barbarians, to wise both and to foolish, a debtor I am;
prose: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.

literal: So the [part] according to me [is] eager also to you, the [ones] in Rome, to preach the gospel.
prose: So, as far as I am concerned, I am eager to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

literal: For not I am ashamed of the gospel, for [it] is power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes, to Jew both [first] and to Greek.
prose: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, since it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

literal: For [the] righteousness of God in it is revealed, from faith to faith, as it has been written: The [one] but righteous by faith will live.
prose: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed, from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous one will live by faith."

literal: For is being revealed wrath of God from heaven upon all ungodliness and wickedness of men, of those the truth in wickedness suppressing,
prose: For the wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth in wickedness,

literal: Because the known-thing of God plain is among them; for God to them made [it] plain.
prose: Because what can be known of God is plain among them, for God has made it plain to them.

literal: For the invisible things of him, from [the] creation of [the] world, by the things made being perceived, are clearly seen, both his eternal power and divinity, unto their being without excuse,
prose: For his invisible qualities—his eternal power and divinity—have been clearly seen ever since the creation of the world, being understood through the things he has made, so that they are without excuse,

literal: because, having known God, not as God did they glorify [him] or give thanks, but they were made vain in their reasonings, and was darkened their senseless heart.
prose: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give him thanks, but became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless hearts were darkened.

literal: Claiming to be wise, they were made foolish,
prose: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,

literal: And they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God in a likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed animals, and of reptiles.
prose: And they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image made in the likeness of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed animals, and of reptiles.

literal: Therefore handed over them the God, in the desires of the hearts of them, unto uncleanness, of the being dishonored the bodies of them among themselves,
prose: Therefore God gave them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies were dishonored among themselves,

literal: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshipped and served the creation beside the one who created [it], who is blessed unto the ages; Amen.
prose: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

literal: For their females exchanged the natural use into that which is contrary to nature,
prose: For their women exchanged natural relations for what is contrary to nature,

literal: And likewise also the males, having abandoned the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their desire toward one another, males with males working out the shamelessness, and receiving back in themselves the recompense which was necessary of their error.
prose: Likewise the men too, abandoning natural relations with women, were inflamed with lust for one another, men committing shameless acts with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.

literal: And just as they did not approve to have God in [full] knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do the things not proper,
prose: And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do the things that are not proper,

literal: having been filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, depravity; whisperers,
prose: filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, depravity; whisperers,

literal: slanderers, God-haters, insolent [ones], arrogant [ones], boasters, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents, senseless,
prose: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, senseless,

literal: Faithless [ones], unloving [ones], unmerciful [ones];
prose: Faithless, unloving, unmerciful.

literal: Who, having known the decree of God, that those practicing such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve of those practicing [them].
prose: Though they know God's decree—that those who practice such things deserve death—they not only do them themselves but also approve of those who practice them.

literal: Therefore without-excuse you-are, O man, every [one] the [one] judging; for in that in which you judge the other, yourself you-condemn, for the same things you-practice, the [one] judging.
prose: Therefore you are without excuse, O man—every one of you who judges. For in that in which you judge the other person, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things.

literal: that the judgment of God is according to truth upon those practicing such things
prose: that God's judgment is according to truth upon those who practice such things

literal: But do you reckon this, O man, the one judging those practicing such things and doing them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?
prose: Do you reckon this, O man who judges those who practice such things and yet do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?

literal: Or of-the riches of-the kindness of-him and of-the forbearance and of-the patience you-despise, not-knowing that the kindness of-the God into repentance you it-leads?
prose: Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God is leading you to repentance?

literal: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you store up for yourself wrath, in a day of wrath and of revelation of righteous judgment of God,
prose: But because of your hardness and unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,

literal: who will render to each one according to his works:
prose: who will render to each one according to his works:

literal: to the [ones] on the one hand according to endurance of good work glory and honor and incorruptibility seeking, eternal life;
prose: to those who seek glory and honor and immortality by perseverance in good work, eternal life;

literal: but to-those out-of contentiousness and disobeying the truth, but obeying unrighteousness—wrath and fury,
prose: but to those who are out of contentiousness and disobey the truth, but obey unrighteousness—wrath and fury,

literal: affliction and distress, upon every soul of-man of-the-one working-out the evil, of-Jew both first and of-Greek;
prose: affliction and distress, upon every soul of man who works out evil, of Jew first and also of Greek;

literal: But glory and honor and peace to everyone the [one] working the good, to Jew both first and to Greek;
prose: But glory and honor and peace to everyone who works what is good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek;

literal: For there is not partiality with God.
prose: For there is no partiality with God.

literal: For as many as sinned without law, without law also will perish; and as many as sinned in [the] law, through [the] law will be judged;
prose: For as many as have sinned without the law will also perish without the law; and as many as have sinned within the law will be judged by the law;

literal: For not the hearers of law [are] righteous before [the] God, but the doers of law will be justified.
prose: For it is not the hearers of law who are righteous before God, but the doers of law will be justified.

literal: For whenever Gentiles, the ones not having law, by nature do the things of the law, these, not having law, are law to themselves;
prose: For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having the law, are a law to themselves;

literal: who show the work of the law [to be] written in their hearts, their conscience bearing-witness-with [them], and between one another their thoughts accusing or also defending [them],
prose: who show that the work of the law is written in their hearts, their conscience bearing joint witness, and their thoughts between one another accusing or even defending them,

literal: in which day God judges the hidden things of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus
prose: on the day when God judges the hidden things of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus

literal: If but you a Jew are named, and rest upon [the] law, and boast in God,
prose: But if you call yourself a Jew, and rely on the law, and boast in God,

literal: and know the will [of him], and approve the things that differ, being instructed out of the law,
prose: and know his will, and approve the things that excel, being instructed out of the law,

literal: and have been persuaded [that] yourself a guide are of [the] blind, a light of those in darkness,
prose: and are persuaded that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those in darkness,

literal: an instructor of [the] foolish, a teacher of infants, having the form of knowledge and of truth in the law —
prose: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and of truth —

literal: The one preaching not to steal, do you steal?
prose: You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

literal: The one saying not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? The one abhorring the idols, do you rob temples?
prose: You who say that one must not commit adultery—do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

literal: You who in [the] law boast, through the transgression of the law do you dishonor God?
prose: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God through your transgression of the law?

literal: For the name of God because of you is blasphemed among the Gentiles, just as it has been written.
prose: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, just as it is written.

literal: For circumcision indeed benefits, if you practice [the] law; if but a transgressor of law you are, the circumcision of you uncircumcision has become.
prose: For circumcision is indeed of benefit if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

literal: If then the uncircumcision should keep the righteous-requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned unto circumcision?
prose: If then the uncircumcision keeps the righteous requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?

literal: And will-judge the out-of nature uncircumcision the law fulfilling you, the through letter and circumcision transgressor of-law.
prose: And the uncircumcision that is by nature, if it fulfills the law, will judge you, who with letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law.

literal: For not the [one] in the-outward [is] Jew is, nor the in the-outward in flesh circumcision [is];
prose: For it is not the one who is a Jew outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh;

literal: But the [one] in the hidden [is] a Jew, and circumcision of heart in spirit, not in letter, of whom the praise [is] not from men but from God.
prose: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; his praise is not from men but from God.

literal: What then [is] the advantage of the Jew, or what [is] the benefit of circumcision?
prose: What advantage, then, does the Jew have, or what is the benefit of circumcision?

literal: Much according to every way. First indeed [for] because they were entrusted the oracles of the God.
prose: Much in every way; first of all, because they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

literal: For what? If some were unfaithful, will the unfaithfulness of them the faithfulness of God nullify?
prose: For what? If some were unfaithful, will their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?

literal: But let God be true, and every man a liar, just as it has been written: "So that you might be justified in your words, and you will prevail in your being judged."
prose: But let God be true, and every man a liar, as it is written: "That you may be justified in your words, and may prevail when you are judged."

literal: But if our unrighteousness commends [the] righteousness of God, what shall we say? [Is] not unjust God, the one inflicting the wrath? According to man I speak.
prose: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unjust to inflict wrath? I am speaking in human terms.

literal: May it not be! Since, how will God judge the world?
prose: Certainly not! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?

literal: But if the truth of God abounded in my falsehood to his glory, why am I still also, as a sinner, being judged,
prose: But if God's truth abounded through my falsehood to his glory, why am I still being judged as a sinner?

literal: And not as we are blasphemed, [and] as some say [that] we say, 'Let us do the evil things, in order that the good things may come'? Of whom the judgment just is.
prose: And why not say, as we are slanderously reported and as some claim we say, 'Let us do evil things so that good things may come'? Their condemnation is just.

literal: What then? Are we at an advantage? Not altogether, for we previously charged Jews both and Greeks all [that they] are under sin,
prose: What then? Are we at any advantage? Not at all; for we have already charged that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin,

literal: just as it has been written, that: Not is [there] righteous, not even one; not is [there] understanding [one],
prose: as it is written: There is no righteous person, not even one; there is no one who understands;

literal: Not is [there] seeking-out the God.
prose: There is no one who seeks after God.

literal: All turned away, together they were made worthless; there is not [one] doing goodness, there is not [one] up to one.
prose: All turned away, together they became worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.

literal: [The] throat [is] an opened [grave], the throat of them, with the tongues of them they were deceiving, venom of asps [is] under the lips of them,
prose: Their throat is an opened grave, with their tongues they kept deceiving, the venom of asps is under their lips,

literal: of whom the mouth of cursing and of bitterness is full;
prose: whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;

literal: Swift [are] the feet of them to shed blood,
prose: Their feet are swift to shed blood,

literal: ruin and misery [are] in their ways,
prose: ruin and misery are in their paths,
